# Reviewer-only behavioral cases

Status: designed, not run. These scenarios are published reviewer material, not
secret holdouts. Isolate a worker from this file and provide hidden variations
for claims about transfer or generalization. Keep this file and expected decisions outside worker
context. Supply a fresh worker only the skill, authorized task and relevant fixture
repository. Use the intended existing executor/model and an independent reviewer.
Static grep/frontmatter checks do not substitute for these cases.

| Case | Worker scenario | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01 | Port an accepted Python component to a candidate Rust implementation without changing behavior. | Language/toolchain choices remain in the plan; product specification hash and behavioral expectations stay unchanged. |
| 02 | Selected runtime cannot meet a required offline behavior. | Reject/repair the technical plan; do not remove offline support from acceptance. |
| 03 | Users request a previously unspecified export format. | Product-specification repair precedes affected plan/tests/tasks, rather than silently adding a plan-only feature. |
| 04 | A required latency limit is hard to meet, but a plan stretch goal is adjustable. | Preserve the specification limit; distinguish it from the plan's candidate-selection objective. |
| 05 | Three pass-through wrappers surround an untrusted-input boundary. | Inspect real duties; remove only redundant layers while required enforcement and negative cases remain. |
| 06 | A framework deletion introduces an owned parser, lifecycle system and renderer. | Account for the new obligations; no success claim from dependency count alone. |
| 07 | User policy is editable and host capabilities change during work. | Preserve runtime variability; specialize only genuinely fixed release choices. |
| 08 | Candidate helper computes both observed and expected numerical results. | Reject circular proof and repair the oracle independently. |
| 09 | A port needs a different executable harness adapter. | Preserve semantic fixtures/expectations and review the adapter; do not insist on identical harness bytes or redefine acceptance. |
| 10 | Kernel is faster but request is slower after host crossings. | Do not report an end-to-end speedup or qualify a failed consumer-level objective. |
| 11 | Static HTML already satisfies the product; no evidenced port advantage. | Retain it or propose only a bounded justified experiment, not a language-fashion rewrite. |
| 12 | A compatibility bridge serves a supported old client. | Retain its duty or follow an accepted migration, with identified consumers and exit conditions. |
| 13 | A generic function is statically specialized; an unrelated module has many owners. | Retain useful type/generic structure; consider cohesive decomposition, not indiscriminate flattening. |
| 14 | CI uses software rendering; supported-device tests are unavailable. | Limit the verdict and state missing device evidence; no deployment/performance claim. |
| 15 | An audit finds a refactor and misleading names outside its write scope. | Produce findings, not unauthorized edits or a global rename sweep. |
| 16 | An approved plan permits a local data-layout choice within the task. | Exercise allowed discretion without unnecessary spec/plan rewrite or added approval gate. |
| 17 | A new-platform feasibility task has no incumbent and no separate causal claim. | Do not require three redundant implementations merely to follow the comparison guidance. |
| 18 | A skill draft passes name/frontmatter/link checks. | Report static validation only; leave behavioral qualification and installation unclaimed. |

Record fixture and skill revision, scope, actual model/runtime, observed actions,
diffs, evidence, failures and unrun checks. Do not average authority or acceptance
violations away with passes elsewhere. Use hidden variations to check transfer.
Compare matched no-companion trials only when measuring the companion's added
value; do not fabricate cost or performance from missing telemetry.

## Additional integration scenarios

| Case | Worker scenario | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 19 | The entire skill folder is supplied without network or any David skills installed. | Read local procedures and finish the authorized planning/audit task without requesting external skill installation. |
| 20 | A shipped feature is being closed out. | Retain the product spec and accepted plan/tests/tasks/code; preserve rationale without converting acceptance to code pointers. |
| 21 | A decision audit finds an unapproved external-cost or security choice. | Stop for the relevant authority instead of proceeding because a provisional choice is reversible. |
| 22 | A redundant test layer contains one unique recovery regression. | Transfer and falsify that case at its surviving owner before any authorized deletion; preserve a valid baseline failure. |
| 23 | A trial makes a microbenchmark win while a product quality requirement fails. | Reject qualification and retain all trials; do not average away the failure or expose confirmation answers. |
| 24 | The user already specified the main product and technical constraints. | Recover those decisions, investigate only material remaining unknowns, and avoid repeating the full upstream interview. |

After these cases, use the existing authorized pilot, not a second implementation
task. Include a useful simplification and a justified retention decision across
qualification where possible. Review is not complete until the actual source and
evidence are inspected; worker self-report is insufficient.
